Relay-shed notebook · recovered fragments

Field Logs

These are the five entries that survived the fire of December 1997. They are reproduced exactly as written, in the order they appear in the notebook — by shift, never rearranged. Operators recorded the date, the band conditions, and whatever came up the antenna that they could not explain. Read them carefully. They were left for someone. Perhaps for you.

Northwind, and a number that was not random

A. Holloway · 1988-11-03 · band: turbulent · S5 fading to S2

Came on shift at 23:00 to a hard northwind rattling the guy-wires. Carrier steady at our frequency. At 01:14 a woman's voice, flat, counted in groups of five for nineteen minutes: 14 7 7 0 · 14 7 7 0 · stand by · stand by It was not a numbers station I knew. It read back our own frequency to us, over and over, as if to say: we know exactly where you are listening from. I logged it and did not sleep.

Margin, in pencil: "she knew the dial. how does the band know the dial?"

Interlace patterns over the dead band

M. Reyes · 1991-02-17 · band: dead · S0

Nothing on the band tonight, which is the worst kind of night, because the longwave is never truly empty — emptiness on the dial means something is masking. At 02:40 the static interlaced: two layers of hiss, slightly out of phase, beating against each other in a slow rhythm. If you closed your eyes it sounded like breathing. I timed the breaths. They matched mine. When I held my breath, the band held its breath. I am not putting my name to a theory. I am only putting it to the log.

Groundwave bleed, transcription unreadable

D. Okafor · 1993-08-29 · band: unstable · transcription flagged corrupt by archivist

The duty operator's transcription for this night was filed as corrupted text and never restored. It is reproduced here verbatim, character for character, in the hope that a future listener can recover it. The archivist's only note reads: "this is not corruption. it is a habit. we always shifted the names."

vs lbh ner ernqvat guvf, gur jngpu vf lbhef abj. gur bcrengbe ba qhgl gbavtug jnf zr. gur anzr lbh jnag, gur anzr gung bcraf gur grezvany, vf ZL anzr: ubyybjnl. gur erprvire vgfrys vf anzrq va gur gvgyrf nobir — svefg yrggref, gbc gb obggbz.

Hint preserved for restorers: a Caesar shift of thirteen places (ROT13) returns plain English.

Halflight transmission, repeating

S. Lindqvist · 1995-10-02 · band: clear · S7

Best conditions in a year. At the half-light just before dawn a male voice, very calm, read a single line in English on a fourteen-second loop: "the door is the frequency · the key is the name · the name is in the logs" It looped until sunrise, then stopped exactly at first light. I have heard a lot of strange traffic on this dial. I have never heard the dial give instructions. It is almost as if it wants to be solved.

Tidewater silence, and the last shift

A. Holloway · 1997-12-19 · band: — · final entry in the notebook

Last night on the ridge. The cooperative votes to stand down at dawn; the others have already gone home. I am keeping the carrier up one more night out of stubbornness. The band is silent the way the tide is silent at the turn — full of something held back. I have written everything a future operator needs into these five logs. The name is here. The receiver is here. The frequency is on every page we ever printed. Whoever you are: you will not be alone on this dial. We are still on it. We are just very far away now.

End of recovered notebook. The carrier, per the log, was never switched off.
